# miniserve - serve files and directories over HTTP

miniserve is a small command-line tool that serves files and directories over HTTP. It is intended for
quick ad-hoc sharing of files from a machine on a network.

Usage examples

Serve a directory:

    miniserve /path/to/directory

Serve a single file:

    miniserve /path/to/file.iso

Set a custom index file:

    miniserve --index index.html /path/to/directory

Serve a Single Page Application (forward non-existent paths to the SPA index):

    miniserve --spa --index index.html /path/to/spa

Require username/password:

    miniserve --auth user:password /path/to/directory

Start with TLS:

    miniserve --tls-cert /path/to/cert.pem --tls-key /path/to/key.pem /path/to/directory

Upload a file using curl (when upload support is enabled):

    # in one terminal
    miniserve -u -- .
    # in another terminal
    curl -F "path=@$FILE" http://localhost:8080/upload\?path\=/

For a full list of available options and flags, consult the tool's built-in help:

    miniserve --help

          [env: MINISERVER_TEMP_UPLOAD_DIRECTORY=]

      --index <INDEX>
          The name of a directory index file to serve, like "index.html"
          
          Normally, when miniserve serves a directory, it creates a listing for that directory.
          However, if a directory contains this file, miniserve will serve that file instead.
          
          [env: MINISERVE_INDEX=]

          Activate SPA (Single Page Application) mode
          
          This will cause the file given by --index to be served for all non-existing file paths. In
          effect, this will serve the index file whenever a 404 would otherwise occur in order to
          allow the SPA router to handle the request instead.
          
          [env: MINISERVE_SPA=]

          Activate Pretty URLs mode
          
          This will cause the server to serve the equivalent `.html` file indicated by the path.

          [default: 8080]

def freeport():

class Srv:

        url='http://127.0.0.1:%d%s'%(self.port,path)

        if headers:

        try:
            resp=urllib.request.urlopen(r)
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
            resp=e
        hdrs=[(k.lower(),v if isinstance(v,bytes) else v.encode()) for k,v in resp.headers.items()]
        body=resp.read()
        return resp.status, hdrs, body
    def show(self,path,**kw):
        st,h,b=self.req(path,**kw)
        print("=== %s -> %d"%(path,st))
        for k,v in h: print("  %s: %s"%(k,v.decode() if isinstance(v,bytes) else v))

        else: print("  BODY: (%d bytes) %s..."%(len(b),b[:200]))
        return st,h,b
    def stop(self):
        self.p.terminate()

{"command": "cd /workspace && cat > src/cli.rs <<'EOF'
use clap::builder::{ArgAction, Arg, Command, PossibleValue, ValueHint};

pub const VERSION: &str = "0.32.0";
pub const NAME: &str = "miniserve";
pub const ABOUT: &str = "For when you really just want to serve some files over HTTP right now!";

pub fn command() -> Command {
    Command::new(NAME)
        .version(VERSION)
        .about(ABOUT)
        .arg(
            Arg::new("path")
                .value_name("PATH")
                .env("MINISERVE_PATH")
                .help("Which path to serve")
                .value_hint(ValueHint::AnyPath),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("verbose")
                .short('v')
                .long("verbose")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Be verbose, includes emitting access logs")
                .env("MINISERVE_VERBOSE"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("temp_directory")
                .long("temp-directory")
                .value_name("TEMP_UPLOAD_DIRECTORY")
                .help(
                    "The path to where file uploads will be written to before being moved to their correct location. It's wise to make sure that this directory will be written to disk and not into memory.",
                )
                .long_help(
                    "The path to where file uploads will be written to before being moved to their correct location. It's wise to make sure that this directory will be written to disk and not into memory.\n\nThis value will only be used **IF** file uploading is enabled. If this option is not set, the operating system default temporary directory will be used.",
                )
                .env("MINISERVER_TEMP_UPLOAD_DIRECTORY")
                .value_hint(ValueHint::DirPath),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("index")
                .long("index")
                .value_name("INDEX")
                .help("The name of a directory index file to serve, like \"index.html\"")
                .long_help(
                    "The name of a directory index file to serve, like \"index.html\"\n\nNormally, when miniserve serves a directory, it creates a listing for that directory. However, if a directory contains this file, miniserve will serve that file instead.",
                )
                .env("MINISERVE_INDEX")
                .value_hint(ValueHint::FilePath),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("spa")
                .long("spa")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Activate SPA (Single Page Application) mode")
                .long_help(
                    "Activate SPA (Single Page Application) mode\n\nThis will cause the file given by --index to be served for all non-existing file paths. In effect, this will serve the index file whenever a 404 would otherwise occur in order to allow the SPA router to handle the request instead.",
                )
                .env("MINISERVE_SPA"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("pretty_urls")
                .long("pretty-urls")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Activate Pretty URLs mode")
                .long_help(
                    "Activate Pretty URLs mode\n\nThis will cause the server to serve the equivalent `.html` file indicated by the path.\n\n`/about` will try to find `about.html` and serve it.",
                )
                .env("MINISERVE_PRETTY_URLS"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("port")
                .short('p')
                .long("port")
                .value_name("PORT")
                .help("Port to use")
                .env("MINISERVE_PORT")
                .default_value("8080"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("interfaces")
                .short('i')
                .long("interfaces")
                .value_name("INTERFACES")
                .action(ArgAction::Append)
                .help("Interface to listen on")
                .env("MINISERVE_INTERFACE")
                .value_hint(ValueHint::AnyPath),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("auth")
                .short('a')
                .long("auth")
                .value_name("AUTH")
                .action(ArgAction::Append)
                .help("Set authentication")
                .long_help(
                    "Set authentication\n\nCurrently supported formats:\nusername:password, username:sha256:hash, username:sha512:hash\n(e.g. joe:123,\njoe:sha256:a665a45920422f9d417e4867efdc4fb8a04a1f3fff1fa07e998e86f7f7a27ae3)",
                )
                .env("MINISERVE_AUTH"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("auth_file")
                .long("auth-file")
                .value_name("AUTH_FILE")
                .help("Read authentication values from a file")
                .long_help(
                    "Read authentication values from a file\n\nExample file content:\n\njoe:123\nbob:sha256:a665a45920422f9d417e4867efdc4fb8a04a1f3fff1fa07e998e86f7f7a27ae3\nbill:",
                )
                .env("MINISERVE_AUTH_FILE")
                .value_hint(ValueHint::FilePath),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("route_prefix")
                .long("route-prefix")
                .value_name("ROUTE_PREFIX")
                .help("Use a specific route prefix")
                .env("MINISERVE_ROUTE_PREFIX"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("random_route")
                .long("random-route")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Generate a random 6-hexdigit route")
                .env("MINISERVE_RANDOM_ROUTE"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("no_symlinks")
                .short('P')
                .long("no-symlinks")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Hide symlinks in listing and prevent them from being followed")
                .env("MINISERVE_NO_SYMLINKS"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("hidden")
                .short('H')
                .long("hidden")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Show hidden files")
                .env("MINISERVE_HIDDEN"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("default_sorting_method")
                .short('S')
                .long("default-sorting-method")
                .value_name("DEFAULT_SORTING_METHOD")
                .help("Default sorting method for file list")
                .value_parser(clap::builder::EnumValueParser::<SortMethod>::new())
                .default_value("name")
                .env("MINISERVE_DEFAULT_SORTING_METHOD"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("default_sorting_order")
                .short('O')
                .long("default-sorting-order")
                .value_name("DEFAULT_SORTING_ORDER")
                .help("Default sorting order for file list")
                .value_parser(clap::builder::EnumValueParser::<SortOrder>::new())
                .default_value("desc")
                .env("MINISERVE_DEFAULT_SORTING_ORDER"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("color_scheme")
                .short('c')
                .long("color-scheme")
                .value_name("COLOR_SCHEME")
                .help("Default color scheme")
                .possible_values(COLOR_SCHEMES.iter().map(|c| PossibleValue::new(*c)))
                .default_value("squirrel")
                .env("MINISERVE_COLOR_SCHEME"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("color_scheme_dark")
                .short('d')
                .long("color-scheme-dark")
                .value_name("COLOR_SCHEME_DARK")
                .help("Default color scheme")
                .possible_values(COLOR_SCHEMES.iter().map(|c| PossibleValue::new(*c)))
                .default_value("archlinux")
                .env("MINISERVE_COLOR_SCHEME_DARK"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("qrcode")
                .short('q')
                .long("qrcode")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Enable QR code display")
                .env("MINISERVE_QRCODE"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("upload_files")
                .short('u')
                .long("upload-files")
                .value_name("ALLOWED_UPLOAD_DIR")
                .num_args(0..=1)
                .help("Enable file uploading (and optionally specify for which directory)")
                .long_help(
                    "Enable file uploading (and optionally specify for which directory)\n\nThe provided path is not a physical file system path. Instead, it's relative to the serve dir. For instance, if the serve dir is '/home/hello', set this to '/upload' to allow uploading to '/home/hello/upload'. When specified via environment variable, a path always needs to be specified.",
                )
                .env("MINISERVE_ALLOWED_UPLOAD_DIR")
                .value_hint(ValueHint::AnyPath),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("web_upload_files_concurrency")
                .long("web-upload-files-concurrency")
                .value_name("WEB_UPLOAD_CONCURRENCY")
                .help(
                    "Configure amount of concurrent uploads when visiting the website. Must have upload-files option enabled for this setting to matter.",
                )
                .long_help(
                    "Configure amount of concurrent uploads when visiting the website. Must have upload-files option enabled for this setting to matter.\n\nFor example, a value of 4 would mean that the web browser will only upload 4 files at a time to the web server when using the web browser interface.\n\nWhen the value is kept at 0, it attempts to resolve all the uploads at once in the web browser.\n\nNOTE: Web pages have a limit of how many active HTTP connections that they can make at one time, so even though you might set a concurrency limit of 100, the browser might only make progress on the max amount of connections it allows the web page to have open.",
                )
                .default_value("0")
                .env("MINISERVE_WEB_UPLOAD_CONCURRENCY"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("chmod")
                .long("chmod")
                .value_name("CHMOD")
                .help("Set unix file permissions of uploaded files")
                .long_help(
                    "Set unix file permissions of uploaded files\n\nThis takes an octal number, for example 0600. By default 0666 & ~umask is used to simulate the system's default behavior.",
                )
                .env("MINISERVE_CHMOD"),
        )
        .arg(

                .long("directory-size")

pub fn is_tty() -> bool {

/// Read random bytes from the operating system.
pub fn rand_bytes(buf: &mut [u8]) {
    if let Ok(mut f) = std::fs::File::open("/dev/urandom") {
        use std::io::Read;
        if f.read_exact(buf).is_ok() {
            return;
        }
    }
    // fallback: time based
    let mut seed = std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map(|d| d.as_nanos() as u64)
        .unwrap_or(12345);
    for b in buf.iter_mut() {
        seed = seed.wrapping_mul(6364136223846793005).wrapping_add(1442695040888963407);
        *b = (seed >> 33) as u8;
    }
}

pub fn mime_type(path: &std::path::Path) -> (&'static str, bool) {

/// Content disposition following actix-web's NamedFile rules.
pub fn disposition(mime: &str) -> &'static str {
    if mime.starts_with("text/")
        || mime.starts_with("image/")
        || mime.starts_with("audio/")
        || mime.starts_with("video/")
        || mime == "application/json"
        || mime == "application/javascript"

    {

    } else {

        self.0.insert_str(0, initial);

        let mut line_sep = "\n".to_owned();
        line_sep.push_str(trailing);

    #[cfg(all(not(feature = "wrap_help"), feature = "help"))]
    pub(crate) fn wrap(&mut self, _hard_width: usize) {}

    #[cfg(feature = "wrap_help")]
    pub(crate) fn wrap(&mut self, hard_width: usize) {
        let mut new = String::with_capacity(self.0.len());

        let mut last = 0;
        let mut wrapper = crate::output::textwrap::wrap_algorithms::LineWrapper::new(hard_width);
        for content in self.iter_text() {
            // Preserve styling
            let current = content.as_ptr() as usize - self.0.as_str().as_ptr() as usize;
            if last != current {
                new.push_str(&self.0.as_str()[last..current]);
            }
            last = current + content.len();

            for (i, line) in content.split_inclusive('\n').enumerate() {
                if 0 < i {
                    // reset char count on newline, skipping the start as we might have carried
                    // over from a prior block of styled text
                    wrapper.reset();
                }
                let line = crate::output::textwrap::word_separators::find_words_ascii_space(line)
    }

    pub fn render_options_section(&self, w: &mut dyn Write) -> Result<(), std::io::Error> {
        let mut roff = Roff::default();
        self._render_options_section(&mut roff);
        roff.to_writer(w)
    }

    fn _render_options_section(&self, roff: &mut Roff) {
        let help_headings = self
            .cmd
            .get_arguments()
            .filter(|a| !a.is_hide_set())
            .filter_map(|arg| arg.get_help_heading())
            .fold(vec![], |mut acc, header| {
                if !acc.contains(&header) {
                    acc.push(header);
                }

                acc
            });

        let (args, mut args_with_heading) =
            self.cmd
                .get_arguments()
                .filter(|a| !a.is_hide_set())
                .partition::<Vec<_>, _>(|a| a.get_help_heading().is_none());

        if !args.is_empty() {
            roff.control("SH", ["OPTIONS"]);
            render::options(roff, &args);
        }

        for heading in help_headings {
            let args;
            (args, args_with_heading) = args_with_heading
                .into_iter()
                .partition(|&a| a.get_help_heading() == Some(heading));

            roff.control("SH", [heading.to_uppercase().as_str()]);
            render::options(roff, &args);
        }
    }

        let mut roff = Roff::default();
        self._render_subcommands_section(&mut roff);

fn option_help(opt: &Arg) -> Option<&clap::builder::StyledStr> {
    if !opt.is_hide_long_help_set() {
        let long_help = opt.get_long_help();
        if long_help.is_some() {
            return long_help;
        }
    }
    if !opt.is_hide_short_help_set() {
        return opt.get_help();
    }

    None
}

fn option_environment(_opt: &Arg) -> Option<Vec<Inline>> {
    #[cfg(feature = "env")]
    {
        let opt = _opt;
        if opt.is_hide_env_set() {
            return None;
        } else if let Some(env) = opt.get_env() {
            return Some(vec![
                roman("May also be specified with the "),
                bold(env.to_string_lossy().into_owned()),
                roman(" environment variable. "),
            ]);
        }
    }

    None
}

fn option_default_values(opt: &Arg) -> Option<String> {

fn format_possible_values(possibles: &Vec<&clap::builder::PossibleValue>) -> Vec<Roff> {
    let mut lines = vec![];
    for value in possibles {
        let mut roff = Roff::default();
        let val_name = value.get_name();
        match value.get_help() {
            Some(help) => {
                roff.text([roman(format!("{val_name}: {help}"))]);
            }
            None => {
                roff.text([roman(val_name.to_owned())]);
            }
        }
        lines.push(roff);
    }
    lines
}

fn subcommand_sort_key(command: &clap::Command) -> (usize, &str) {
    (command.get_display_order(), command.get_name())
}

/// Note that this function is duplicated from `clap::builder`
fn option_sort_key(arg: &Arg) -> (usize, String) {
    let key = if let Some(x) = arg.get_short() {
        let mut s = x.to_ascii_lowercase().to_string();
        s.push(if x.is_ascii_lowercase() { '0' } else { '1' });
        s
    } else if let Some(x) = arg.get_long() {
        x.to_string()
    } else {
        let mut s = '{'.to_string();
        s.push_str(arg.get_id().as_str());
        s
    };
    (arg.get_display_order(), key)
}
</output>

/// Raw deflate stream (no zlib/gzip header)
use std::io::Write as _;
pub fn deflate_raw(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut e = flate2::write::DeflateEncoder::new(Vec::new(), flate2::Compression::default());
    let _ = e.write_all(data);
    match e.finish() {
        Ok(v) => v,
        Err(_) => data.to_vec(),
    }
}

/// gzip compressed data with a header matching the reference implementation
pub fn gzip(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut out: Vec<u8> = vec![0x1f, 0x8b, 0x08, 0x00, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0x04, 0xff];
    let mut e = flate2::write::DeflateEncoder::new(Vec::new(), flate2::Compression::best());
    let _ = e.write_all(data);
    match e.finish() {
        Ok(mut v) => {
            out.append(&mut v);
            let mut h = crc32fast::Hasher::new();
            h.update(data);
            let crc = h.finalize();
            out.extend_from_slice(&crc.to_le_bytes());
            out.extend_from_slice(&(data.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
            out
        }
        Err(_) => data.to_vec(),
    }
}

/// Percent-encode a path component like actix/percent-encoding does (non-alphanumeric
/// and not in the RFC 3986 unreserved/sub-delims set get escaped).
pub fn percent_encode_path(s: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len());
    for b in s.as_bytes() {
        let c = *b as char;
        if b.is_ascii_alphanumeric()
            || matches!(b, b'-' | b'_' | b'.' | b'~' | b'!' | b'$' | b'&' | b'\'' | b'(' | b')' | b'*' | b'+' | b',' | b';' | b'=' | b':' | b'@')
        {
            out.push(c);
        } else {
            out.push_str(&format!("%{:02X}", b));
        }
    }
    out
}

        }
    };
    let rel = crate::http::url_decode(&dir);
    let full = state
        .cfg
        .path
        .join(crate::util::normalize_rel(&rel).trim_start_matches('/'));

        let msg = "Invalid HTTP request\ncaused by: Invalid value for 'path' parameter";

fn place_data(m: &mut Matrix, data: &[u8]) {
    let size = m.size as isize;
    let mut bit_idx = 0usize;
    let total_bits = data.len() * 8;
    let mut i = 0isize;
    while i >= 0 {
        for dy in 0..size {
            let y = if (i / 2) % 2 == 0 {
                size - 1 - dy
            } else {
                dy
            };
            for dx in 0..2 {
                let x = i - dx;
                if x < 0 {
                    continue;
                }
                if m.function[y as usize * m.size + x as usize] {
                    continue;
                }
                let dark = if bit_idx < total_bits {
                    let byte = data[bit_idx / 8];
                    (byte >> (7 - (bit_idx % 8))) & 1 == 1
                } else {
                    false
                };
                m.modules[y as usize * m.size + x as usize] = dark;
                bit_idx += 1;
            }
        }
        i -= 2;
    }
}

#!/bin/bash
# Build miniserve. All dependencies are vendored in ./vendor so the build works offline.
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
export CARGO_HOME="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}"
if [ ! -d "$CARGO_HOME" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$CARGO_HOME"
fi
cargo build --release --offline
cp -f target/release/miniserve ./executable
chmod +x ./executable
EOF
chmod +x compile.sh && cat > .gitignore <<'EOF'
target/
executable
nohup.out
EOF
cat > AGENT_REPORT.md <<'MDEOF'
# miniserve reimplementation - status report

## What is implemented
A from-scratch Rust reimplementation of `miniserve 0.32.0` (no original source consulted;
everything was derived by running the provided `./executable` and inspecting its output).

* CLI: built with `clap` (vendored), reproduces `--help`, `-h`, `--version`,
  `--print-manpage` and `--print-completions` for all five shells byte for byte
  (the zsh generator needed a one-line local adjustment in the vendored crate so that
  optional-valued options omit their value spec, as the original does).
* HTTP server: hand written HTTP/1.1 implementation (thread per connection,
  keep-alive, TLS through OpenSSL FFI via `src/tls.rs`).
* Directory listing page: byte-identical to the original for all flag combinations
  that were tested (sorting, hidden files, symlinks, dirs-first, title, footers,
  theme selector, size display, wget footer, external URL, directory size, README,
  index, pretty-urls, SPA, route prefix, custom headers, QR code, ...).
* Sorting quirks reproduced exactly (name order inverted, "ascending" reverses the
  directory order before a stable sort, directories first partitions the entries).
* Relative ("history") times, human sizes, date formats reproduced.
* File serving: content types, content-disposition, etag, last-modified, 304,
  range requests, HEAD.
* Archives: `.tar` and `.zip` generation is byte identical to the original.
* Uploads, mkdir, rm: error/status codes and bodies match.
* Directory-size API (`/__miniserve_internal/api`) with serde-like JSON error messages.
* WebDAV PROPFIND answers the same 403 XML body.
* Error pages (404/400/403/500) match, including the multi-paragraph messages.

## Known differences / TODO
* `.tar.gz` (and `--compress-response`) use a different deflate implementation than
  the original, so the compressed byte stream differs (the container header, CRC and
  sizes are correct, so the archives are valid and extract to identical content).
* The QR code (-q) is generated by a from-scratch encoder; the version/data segments
  are correct but the chosen mask and therefore the final matrix can differ from the
  original. Remaining work: match the mask-selection penalty scoring of the
  `qrcode` crate (the penalty implementation in `src/qr.rs` needs a closer look -
  the data placement direction was already fixed to follow the standard zigzag).
* `--tls-cert/--tls-key` report errors with a different panic message than the
  original (rustls based) - TLS itself works through OpenSSL.
* `-v` access logs are produced in the same format but the actix-internal INFO
  chatter (worker startup/shutdown lines) is only partially reproduced.

## Build
`./compile.sh` builds `target/release/miniserve` and copies it to `./executable`.
All dependencies are vendored in `./vendor` (plus a small local `terminal_size`
stub crate in `terminal_size_stub/`), so the build works without network access.
MDEOF
ls -la; git status --short | head -5
